messages.text: McDermott blasts 'harsh' RL World Cup format

metadata.summary: England head coach Brian McDermott has branded the format of the Rugby League World Cup as "harsh" with his side up against it to progress.
metadata.content: Rugby League World Cup: England head coach Brian McDermot blasts 'harsh' format and explains Mikey Lewis absence | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Rugby League World Cup: England head coach Brian McDermot blasts 'harsh' format and explains Mikey Lewis absence England take on France in Perth on Saturday (7.35am) in their second Rugby League World Cup fixture, having been thrashed by Tonga in opener; Coach Brian McDermott discussed World Cup format and Mikey Lewis' continued absence ahead of weekend clash Thursday 22 October 2026 15:22, UK Image: England coach Brian McDermott has branded the Rugby League World Cup format 'harsh,' with his side up against it to progress England head coach Brian McDermott has branded the format of the Rugby League World Cup as "harsh" with his side up against it to progress. Last Saturday's loss to Tonga means England must hope Tonga beat Samoa in their final group game next week in order to stand any realistic chance of reaching the semi-finals. That scenario would leave England and Samoa to be separated by points difference - a particularly tough ask for McDermott's men given the Samoans started their campaign with a crushing 78-4 win over France. "The jeopardy is losing one game is so harsh, it's almost like we don't get another chance to straighten things out," said McDermott, whose side face the French in their second group game in Perth on Saturday. messages.text: How will Arsenal cope without Saka?

metadata.summary: An innocuous swing of his left boot, a "sharp pain" in his quadriceps, and now an anxious wait for Arsenal. Bukayo Saka's injury was a blot on a positive night against Bayern Munich.
metadata.content: How will Arsenal cope without injured Bukayo Saka? Noni Madueke and Max Dowman in frame for more minutes | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis How will Arsenal cope without injured Bukayo Saka? Noni Madueke and Max Dowman in frame for more minutes Bukayo Saka could face a spell on the sidelines after suffering an injury in Arsenal's 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League, so who will step up in his absence? Nick Wright Football Features Writer @nicholaspwright Thursday 22 October 2026 13:03, UK Image: Bukayo Saka limped off early in Arsenal's Champions League meeting with Bayern Munich An innocuous swing of his left boot, a "sharp pain" in his quadriceps, and now an anxious wait for Arsenal. Bukayo Saka's injury was a blot on a positive night against Bayern Munich. Mikel Arteta offered a gloomy initial prognosis after his 10th-minute withdrawal, revealing his medical staff were "concerned" and adding that it "doesn't look good at all" in his press conference. The injury is the latest in a string of setbacks for Saka, who was almost always available between 2020/21 and 2023/24 but has struggled with hamstring, Achilles and hip issues since. metadata.summary: This would be a hugely sad way for James Anderson to go out.
metadata.content: James Anderson: Nasser Hussain on England legend not having his Lancashire contract renewed and possible retirement | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content James Anderson: Nasser Hussain on England legend not having his Lancashire contract renewed and possible retirement Former England captain Nasser Hussain reflects on reports that James Anderson’s contract will not be renewed at Lancashire, which would end his 26-year career at his boyhood county and raise questions over the 44-year-old’s future in the sport Nasser Hussain Cricket expert and columnist Thursday 22 October 2026 15:14, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nasser Hussain and Kumar Sangakkara give their thoughts on Lancashire reportingly not set to renew Jimmy Anderson's contract This would be a hugely sad way for James Anderson to go out. Of all the things wrong at Lancashire recently and all the problems they've had, on and off the field, I didn't think Anderson was one of them. He took 50 wickets at an average of 17 last season and is a Lancashire boy through and through. He's still bowling well and obviously he's had a couple of injuries, but when he has played he has still put in performances.
